title: Close a named ball valve and padlock its locking handle
instruction: Close ball valve V-12: turn its handle a quarter turn clockwise, seen from above, to its stop. Slide the handle's locking sleeve toward the valve so it latches, then put your padlock's shackle through the hole in the handle and snap it shut. Do not operate valve V-14.
context: Isolating a line for maintenance means closing its valve and padlocking it closed. Closing the wrong valve, or leaving the right one closed but unlocked, lets the line be reopened onto a worker.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Pipe run: a 1/2 in schedule-40 steel pipe (21.3 mm outside diameter, 48 cm long) runs left-right, its axis 26 cm in front of the bases and 12.0 cm above the table, from 12 cm right to 36 cm left of the midline. It is fixed to the table on two grey plastic stands (3 x 2 cm columns on 8 x 5 x 0.8 cm feet) at 9 cm right and 33 cm left of the midline. Valves: two Milwaukee Valve BA-100 1/2 in bronze two-piece threaded ball valves with the LD locking-lever option (distributor part BA100 LDA 12; body 56 mm end to end), with stems 26 cm in front of the bases: V-12 on the midline, V-14 25 cm left of it. Each has a flat stainless lever (110 x 16 x 2.5 mm, 60 g, yellow vinyl grip 19 x 6 mm on its outer 58 mm) 16.5 cm above the table, turning about its vertical stem between two stops. Both valves are open, levers pointing right along the pipe; closed, a lever points straight at the robot. Each lever carries a stainless locking sleeve (12 mm long, 20 x 8 mm outside) that slides 10 mm along it and starts slid out. A zinc stop plate (44 mm across) sits 10 mm under each lever, with a notch at the open and at the closed stop. Slid in at a stop, the sleeve's tongue drops into the notch and the lever cannot turn. Slid in, the sleeve also uncovers a 9.5 mm square hole in the lever, 40 mm from the stem, just outboard of the sleeve. Valve tags: each valve has an engraved two-ply plastic valve tag (102 x 51 x 1.6 mm, white face, black engraved letters about 28 mm tall reading V-12 or V-14) held by an 8 mm steel strap clamped round the pipe 3.3 cm left of its stem. The strap runs back over the pipe and holds the tag behind the valve: tag centre 6.8 cm behind the stem (32.8 cm in front of the bases), 1.5 cm right of the stem and 15 cm above the table, its long side left-right and its face tilted back 60 degrees from vertical so that it faces the robot and the overhead camera. Padlock: a Master Lock 410 Zenex safety padlock (purple, 410PRP; body 38 x 45 x 19 mm, 6.35 mm steel shackle with 38 mm vertical and 19 mm horizontal clearance; 0.10 kg) stands upright and open (shackle popped up 16 mm, key in the cylinder) on a grey plastic column (1.0 x 1.2 cm, 11.3 cm tall, on a 5 x 5 x 1 cm foot) 17 cm in front of the bases and 15 cm left of the midline. Its legs are side by side left-right, the free (short) leg on the right. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time, V-14's lever turns 10 degrees or more, or V-12's lever, once closed, goes back more than 30 degrees from closed before the padlock is shut. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if V-12's lever has turned 10 degrees or more toward closed; 0.5 if it reaches closed (within 5 degrees of its stop, pointing at the robot); 0.75 if, with the lever closed and its sleeve slid in (within 3 mm of fully in), the padlock's short leg also passes through the lever's hole; 1.0 if the padlock is also shut (shackle latched) through the hole and the after-release check passes. Dropping the padlock is not penalised by itself. After-release check, done once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the padlock for 2 s: pull the sleeve outward along the lever with a spring scale at 10 N and keep pulling; after 2 s also push the lever's grip, 95 mm from the stem, toward open at 32 N (about 3.0 N m) for 2 s. Pass if the lever stays within 15 degrees of closed and the shackle is still through the hole; if not, the score is 0.75. Angles are read from a photo taken from above with a protractor template.
reset_notes: Open the padlock with its key and remove it; slide V-12's sleeve out and turn the lever back to open (pointing right); check V-14 is open with its sleeve out; stand the open padlock back on its column with its short leg on the right. About 1.5 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. The locking chain is geometry (tongue into the stop plate's notch, shackle blocks the sleeve). Lever torque 1.5 N·m, a third of Milwaukee's published 4.5 N·m so one arm can turn it. Hole, sleeve, notch, tongue sizes inferred from drawings. Simplified: flat lever, box colliders, Master Lock 410 latches by a catch with no key, enlarged plastic valve tags; check forces in sim after recording. Details in README.
